attacker.model: claude (Kiro subagent; exact model version not exposed to the agent)

cases.label: percentage discount rounds half away from zero: 1.05 * 0.5 % = 0.00525 -> 0.01, not banker's 0.00
cases.reasoning: T-SQL ROUND(@UnitPrice * @HighestDiscountPercentage / 100.0, 2) rounds half away from zero; PostgreSQL round(numeric,2) must do the same, not round-half-to-even. UnitPrice 1.05 ends in 5 and the product 0.00525 is the half-way-ish case a banker's-rounding conversion would mishandle.

cases.label: deal priced at 19.95 competes with a percentage deal; lowest of all paths wins
cases.reasoning: Three independent lowerings (special unit price, discount amount, discount percentage) are each compared with <; the minimum must win on both engines. 19.95 ends in 5 to exercise decimal(18,2) exactness.

cases.label: pricing date at the maximum date 9999-12-31 equals the deal end date (BETWEEN is inclusive)
cases.reasoning: BETWEEN sd.StartDate AND sd.EndDate is inclusive on both engines; the boundary date 9999-12-31 must compare equal, so the special price applies. A conversion using < EndDate would drop it.

cases.label: a negative discount amount would raise the price, so the < guard must reject it
cases.reasoning: MAX(DiscountAmount) is -5.05; @UnitPrice - (-5.05) = 15.05 which is NOT < @CalculatedPrice, so it must be ignored. A conversion that dropped the guard would return 15.05.

cases.label: StockGroup-scoped deal applies only through the StockItemStockGroups bridge; deal ids are non-contiguous
cases.reasoning: The deal with StockGroupID set applies only when EXISTS a bridge row for (@StockItemID, that group). SpecialDealID runs 1, 3 (a gap) to confirm the key is compared by value, not position.

cases.label: no customer row: BuyingGroupID and CustomerCategoryID stay NULL, so only the OR ... IS NULL deal legs match
cases.reasoning: When CustomerID has no Sales.Customers row, the SELECT @BuyingGroupID = ... leaves both variables NULL; (sd.BuyingGroupID = @BuyingGroupID OR sd.BuyingGroupID IS NULL) then matches only deals whose BuyingGroupID IS NULL. PL/pgSQL SELECT INTO with no row also leaves NULLs.

objections.text: The hand-derived percentage-discount case already exercises the same ROUND-versus-truncation path with a value (2.49875) that rounds to 2.50 but truncates to 2.49. Changing the operands to produce 0.00525 does not attack a different branch or mechanism.

The label says banker's rounding would produce 0.00, but 0.00525 is above the exact 0.005 midpoint and therefore rounds to 0.01 under both half-even and half-away-from-zero rounding. The supplied value does not test the claimed tie-breaking difference.

caught: percentage price truncates instead of rounding
missed: lowest discount amount instead of highest

reasons: mutant adequacy is inadequate (unexplained misses: lowest discount amount instead of highest)
